segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for November 21, 2026.
Today we cover advancements in humanoid grasping, new robot standards from China, and fascinating drone feats.
Tune in for the latest!
From Humanoid.guide, "Siemens and AGIBOT design humanoid grippers from text prompts".

This report details an AI agent workflow developed by Siemens and AGIBOT for designing humanoid robot grippers based on text prompts, demonstrating a method for streamlining complex engineering workflows.
The process involves an AI agent that uses a written task description to select a gripper, modify its geometry within Designcenter, and execute virtual simulations.
This system coordinates various engineering software functions through MCP integration to adapt the design according to specified handling requirements.
The methodology prioritizes the required handling specification over individual printing steps, aiming to simplify the engineering process significantly.
Siemens plans to expand this work by integrating additive manufacturing and automation into an adaptive production cell.
This development indicates a step toward more intuitive, prompt-based design for advanced robotics systems.
From Humanoid.guide, China issues five humanoid robot standards covering testing.

This report details the issuance of five new standards by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology on November 16, 2026, designed to address inconsistencies in capability claims, equipment interfaces, and data management within the humanoid robot sector.
These standards encompass capability assessment, training facilities, training data, integrated electric drive joints, and dexterous hands.
A capability classification standard utilizes six levels, L0 to L5, across four dimensions to establish a detailed profile for development and comparison.
Further standards delineate requirements for training sites, hardware specifications, data lifecycle management, and safety protocols.
This standardization aims to facilitate the comparison and integration of humanoid robots through standardized development parameters.
The establishment of these benchmarks sets a framework for industry-wide development and interoperability in humanoid robotics.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Drone Squeezes Itself to Fit Through Tight Spaces"
details innovative robotic concepts showcasing advancements in physical AI and multi-robot systems.
The feature highlights a drone design capable of folding to fit through confined spaces, alongside soft, snake-like robots known as TeCoBots that can link together.
Further examples presented include the AHEADance humanoid robot, which mimics music, and a novel design for dexterous hands utilizing rigid linkages.
The report also covers frameworks for multi-robot collaboration and the development of autonomous racing drones.
These demonstrations emphasize progress in physical AI, coordinated systems, and human-robot interaction.
This progress indicates continued development in tangible robotics and collaborative artificial intelligence systems.
From The Robot Report, "Medtronic’s Hugo surgical robot ready for bigger operation".
This segment reports on the FDA clearance of the Hugo surgical robot for general surgery procedures in the United States, specifically covering abdominal and lower abdominal operations.
Medtronic's modular system permits surgeons to utilize only the requisite robotic arms, providing flexibility for multi-quadrant procedures.
The platform is being enhanced through the integration of Artificial Intelligence to deliver real-time intraoperative guidance and improve patient outcomes.
Robotic surgery implementation facilitates enhanced surgeon experience by mitigating physical strain and improving visualization via three-dimensional imaging and intuitive controls.
Medtronic is focusing on the cost, training, and support necessary to broaden the global accessibility of this technology.
This development signals further integration of advanced artificial intelligence into medical robotics.
From Robotics & Automation News, Watco expands Intramotev autonomous railcar operations to Texas.
This report details the deployment of TugVolt autonomous railcar technology to a second site in Seadrift, Texas, expanding upon prior work conducted at Watco's Wood River, Illinois terminal.
Intramotev will utilize TugVolt units to manage the switching of railcars within an industrial facility in Seadrift.
This technology has previously been successfully employed at the Watco Wood River site for the movement of soda ash.
Intramotev holds the distinction of being the first company globally to commercially deploy autonomous freight railcars.
This expansion signifies further real-world application of autonomous logistics systems in heavy industrial settings.
Future developments in autonomous freight movement are anticipated to follow this operational extension.
From The Robot Report, MassRobotics launching marine robotics facility on Boston Harbor.
This report details the development of a marine robotics facility at the Boston Fish Pier designed to allow startups to build, launch, and test robots within Boston Harbor.
Construction is underway in partnership with the Massachusetts Port Authority, with the facility scheduled for opening in early 2028.
The facility will incorporate testing equipment, including a water tank and launch gear, facilitating streamlined water testing for marine robotics companies.
This setup establishes a direct connection between prototype development and in-harbor testing, supporting over one hundred global startups with this integrated environment.
This initiative promises to accelerate the innovation cycle within the marine robotics sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, ABB names Wasome winner of China startup challenge for AI automation solution.
This report details the selection of Wasome as the winner of the ABB Startup Challenge China 2026 for an AI automation solution.

The challenge sought AI solutions capable of acting as technical experts for engineers in automation tasks, and the winning entry focused on making automation engineering faster, simpler, and more accessible through artificial intelligence.
ABB experts are slated to collaborate with the Wasome team to develop a market-ready solution for customers.
The winning team was awarded a prize of 200,000 CNY along with growth support from SynerLeap.
This initiative underscores the growing focus on applying artificial intelligence to democratize and streamline complex engineering processes within the automation sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, "How to prototype robot control logic before committing to industrial hardware".

This report details the process of prototyping robot control logic on a microcontroller to sketch sequences and timing before committing to industrial hardware, revealing that testing on constrained boards exposes timing assumptions and potential failures often overlooked during hardware commissioning.

Teams utilizing this method can deliberately test state transitions and handle edge cases that are impractical on live systems, establishing a specification that guides the design of final, safety-rated industrial systems, although prototypes do not account for safety ratings or fieldbus determinism.
This approach mandates a foundational logic test prior to physical implementation across the automation sector.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?"
reports on the challenges in replicating human hand dexterity through robotics and the resulting focus on advanced robotic hand development.

The ability to replicate the dexterity of human hands presents a significant challenge for robotics because achieving this requires complex sensory feedback and predictive modeling, which evolved through a combination of cognitive power and physical dexterity.
Research is currently focused on developing specialized dexterous hands for specific tasks, with substantial global investment directed towards this area.
The pace at which artificial dexterity can be replicated in machines will determine the ultimate impact on labor markets.
The technology sector should monitor advancements in fine motor control systems for future developments.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 Jazzy for macOS (Apple Silicon): release 26.11.20.9, self-contained, Gazebo included, Nav2 up in 78 s".
This report details the availability of a self-contained ROS 2 Jazzy package for macOS running on Apple Silicon, which includes Gazebo and the Nav2 navigation stack.
The development focused on creating a build that is self-contained and resilient to Homebrew updates by bundling necessary libraries.
This specific package achieves a significant improvement in simulation startup time, reducing the time required for a TurtleBot 4 with Nav2 simulation to 78 seconds.
The package integrates essential tools such as Nav2, MoveIt 2, and various middleware, emphasizing tracking official ROS 2 development.
This release establishes a streamlined environment for robotics simulation on Apple Silicon platforms.
Further developments in cross-platform ROS tooling are anticipated.
From Robohub, "Robot Talk Episode 171 – Programming robot behaviour, with Sebastian Castro"
reports on the development of open-source software for robot task planning and behavior with Sebastian Castro.
This session focused on methods for programming the dynamic actions of autonomous machines.
The discussion detailed the process of developing open-source software designed to facilitate robot task planning and behavior.
Castro, an independent roboticist working with NASA's Dexterous Robotics Group, contributed expertise in robotic manipulation and software engineering to this project.
The work involved exploring methodologies for creating adaptable programming frameworks that allow robots to execute complex sequences of tasks effectively.
The episode examined the challenges inherent in translating high-level goals into executable robot commands.
The approach involved developing modular systems for defining and executing behaviors, emphasizing the creation of accessible, open-source tools for the wider robotics community.
The exploration focused on the underlying algorithms necessary for sophisticated robot decision-making and interaction with the physical environment.
This work contributes to the advancement of autonomous systems by providing foundational tools for programming complex robotic behaviors.
Further developments in this area are expected to accelerate the deployment of more capable autonomous machines.
From RoboPapers, "Ep#118: Devol Robotics"
reports on the development of physics-grounded foundation models enabling precise robotic manipulation through the incorporation of force and contact understanding.
Devol Robotics utilizes an Interaction World Model to learn visual-geometric representations that predict stiffness and damping based on interaction geometry.
The Devol-ONE model integrates vision-language understanding, world prediction, and action generation within a single autoregressive framework.
This methodology allows robots to reliably execute complex, compliant tasks by predicting physical dynamics during action planning.
Experiments demonstrated that including physical priors substantially enhanced success rates and efficiency in assembly tasks involving physical contact.
This advancement signals a shift toward more physically realistic and capable robotic systems.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your day is fully optimized.
Keep building those amazing ideas, and I'll catch you in the next update.
Bye for now!
